_comment: Curated orthographic-convention register — the decision-layer input to the
orthographies[] derivation (cli/scripts/derive-orthographies.mjs). NOT WIRED:
that deriver is a standalone pass, not imported by cli/scripts/cldf/project.mjs,
so nothing here reaches a card today. An earlier version of this comment claimed
the wiring existed; it did not. Do not restore that claim before the import does.
ONE entry per language code, keyed by ISO 15924 script code. Each script entry may set
scheme / longVowelMarking / canonicalForMt and MUST set a source string that cites a
verifiable basis — a source the card already carries, a published convention, or a tool
in the repo's register. Only add entries whose convention is actually documented:
absence means unknown, and the deriver writes nothing it cannot cite (index, not
arbiter). Optional keys are OMITTED when unknown, never guessed. Do NOT record measured
scores here — a score of method output is a run result and belongs on the leaderboard.
Data-over-code (docs/AGENTS.md §1): language-specific conventions live in this file,
never hardcoded in the deriver. Decision-layer inputs to the atlas build live under the
monorepo-root shared/ (parameters.csv, card-field-disposition.json, catalogue/…); this
file moved here from cli/shared/ on 2026-09-06 for that reason — cli/shared/ is the
npm-bundled RUNTIME tree, and nothing reads this register at runtime.
STANDING VERDICT (shared/cldf/curated-file-verdicts.json, 2026-08-06):
'CITABLE BUT NOT MACHINE-FETCHABLE — keep, with a bibliographic citation added, and
record that it is asserted from the literature rather than fetched.' Every entry below
is asserted from the literature and from tools the card already lists. None is fetched,
so none carries a pin; that is the reason this is a curated register and not a source.

Latn.source: manual-curation (asserted from the literature and from a tool the card already carries — not machine-fetched). SRO is Standard Roman Orthography for Plains Cree; it writes the seven long vowels with circumflexes (â ê î ô) against unmarked short vowels. AUTHORITY: the GiellaLT / UAlbertaALTLab lang-crk finite-state transducer, which the crk card lists under resources.fsts from the giellalt-resources source (https://github.com/giellalt/lang-crk, https://github.com/UAlbertaALTLab/lang-crk). Both analysers accept the hyphenated preverb spelling (ê-nipâyân, nikî-nipân, kâ-nipât) and return the SAME analysis plus the tag Err/Orth — the FST's own spelling-error tag — for the fused spelling, so 'correct SRO' here is the grammar machine's verdict rather than a house preference. CANONICAL-FOR-MT: crk is written in two scripts and the pipeline's working script is the Roman one (shared/catalogue/card-config.json scriptConverter.crk converts between them); the scripts[] `primary` display flag is NOT this signal. REFERENCE LEXICON, cited and never redistributed (founder ruling 2026-07-19, index-only permanently): Wolvengrey, Arok, ed. 2001. nehiyawewin: itwewina / Cree: Words. Regina: Canadian Plains Research Center.

Cans.source: manual-curation (asserted, not fetched). Unified Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics is an attested writing system for Plains Cree and stays on the card as an alternative — the language is written both ways and an index says so. It is NOT the pipeline's working form: shared/catalogue/card-config.json registers scriptConverter.crk precisely because syllabics is converted to and from the Roman orthography, and the lang-crk analysers cited on the Latn entry above are SRO-facing. longVowelMarking is OMITTED rather than guessed: syllabics marks vowel length by a diacritic over the syllable, which none of the schema's vocabulary terms (circumflex / macron / double-vowel / none) describes.
